name: Swede
grown_as: The swede (rutabaga), a biennial grown as an annual for its large yellow-fleshed root, sown in late spring and lifted from autumn through winter. Drawn as a purple-topped variety such as 'Marian'; some are green- or bronze-topped. ⚠️ CHECK: William's variety.
habit: Year 1: a rosette of leaves 30 to 50 cm high from the top of a large round root with a distinct neck. Year 2: a branched, smooth, waxy flowering stem 60 to 120 cm.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the top of the neck; alternate on the flowering stem
leaf.type: Simple, deeply lobed: lyre-shaped, a large end lobe and several pairs of smaller side lobes
leaf.base: Tapering into the stalk with small lobes. Upper stem leaves undivided and clasping the stem with rounded ears
leaf.veins: A broad pale midrib, side veins netted
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless (a few hairs on the youngest leaves only), with a waxy bloom that rubs off

flower.colour: Pale to buff yellow, paler than turnip
flower.centre: Six stamens (four long, two short) round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow sepals held half upright
flower.carried: In elongated clusters at the branch tips, the unopened buds level with or standing above the open flowers
flower.season: April to May of the second year

fruit: Slender cylindrical pods 5 to 10 cm with a short beak, held up on spreading stalks, splitting to release small round dark brown to black seeds.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip, a little grey-green; first true leaves smooth and grey-green.
winter: Very hardy: roots stand in the ground all winter, the outer leaves yellowing and dying back while a few small grey-green leaves remain on the neck.

leaf: lyre-shaped with a large end lobe and smaller side lobes
smooth and waxy blue-grey green, not bristly
bloom: four pale yellow petals in a cross
buds level with or above the open flowers
seed: a tiny round dark brown to black seed
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip, a little grey-green
young: a rosette of smooth grey-green lobed leaves
the root starting to swell at the soil
crop: a large round root, purple above the soil and creamy yellow below
a distinct neck at the top ringed with leaf scars, the leaves from its tip
a tail root and side roots below
flower: a smooth grey-green branched stem with clasping upper leaves
seedhead: slender upright beaked pods along the stems

look_alikes: Turnip has bristly bright green leaves, white flesh and no neck. Kohlrabi's swelling is the stem above ground, with leaves from its sides. Oilseed rape is the same species with no swollen root.
